basics.summary: I am an AI automation engineer, AI strategist, and consultant. Until August 2026 I worked at Innodata Inc. as an AI Automation Engineer and Analyst, and from January 2026 as acting team lead for AI training. I help identify where AI can create practical leverage, translate business problems into AI solutions, and build working prototypes for real workflows: agentic workflows, RAG systems, research agents, API automations, and human-in-the-loop systems using n8n, Python, LLMs, and local AI. Evaluation is a big part of my work. I test LLM behaviour, retrieval quality, workflow reliability, and automation performance to understand where and why AI systems succeed or fail. I bring the same quantitative toolkit (statistics, time-series modelling, and Bayesian inference) to quantitative analysis and finance. Beyond building, I work across product, growth, and scale: deciding what is worth building, sizing the business case behind it, and leading a team of AI trainers as acting team lead. I think from first principles, and I still run research-paper-based experiments, now on AI agents and the systems built around them. Before industry, I was a pre-doctoral research fellow in theoretical physics at Ahmedabad University. My research focused on compact objects in general relativity, including naked singularities, black-hole mimickers, energy extraction, and high-energy particle collisions, and led to four peer-reviewed papers in journals such as Physical Review D and the European Physical Journal C.

projects.name: AI Stack Advisor: Build-vs-Buy Calculator for AI
projects.description: Describe what you want AI to do, and it compares five ways to get there (buy a SaaS tool, build on hosted LLM APIs, run an open model on your own GPUs, mix the two, or pay per token for a hosted open model) on monthly cost, 36-month total cost of ownership, break-even volume, and ROI. Every assumption is shown, and 300 simulations report how often each option wins. It runs entirely in the browser.

projects.name: Aditi: Hindi + English Real Estate Voice Agent
projects.description: A real-time voice agent for a fictional Ahmedabad real estate agency. The LLM decides which of ten tools to use: it searches listings, works out home-loan EMIs, books, moves, or cancels site visits, and texts the caller a follow-up SMS. Callers can interrupt mid-sentence or switch between Hindi and English mid-call, and it runs on free tiers with backup models and voices.

projects.name: Saati: Personal AI Agent with Long-Term Memory
projects.description: A personal AI agent on Telegram that tracks projects, ideas, and decisions, follows coding sessions and voice notes, and sends morning, evening, and weekly briefings. It runs in the cloud on a Gemini model. Its memory design was tested in two rounds of research-paper-based experiments on real session history.

projects.name: TickerBrief: Automated Equity Research Reports
projects.description: Type a ticker and get a full equity research report as an interactive web page and a PDF. An n8n workflow pulls prices, fundamentals, peers, SEC filings, and news in parallel; Python computes ratios, technical indicators, and sentiment; and a local LLM writes the narrative in three structured passes, with rule-based fallbacks.

projects.name: Model Monitoring + Drift Alert System
projects.description: A local MLOps stack that watches a deployed model. An n8n workflow scores new traffic, logs predictions to Postgres, and measures data, prediction, and target drift with Evidently AI. When a threshold is crossed, a local LLM explains the likely root cause in plain English and posts it to Slack, with a Grafana dashboard for the history.

projects.name: ArXiv Research Analysis Workflow
projects.description: Monitors arXiv every morning (gr-qc and q-fin by default), filters new papers by keyword, and sends a Telegram brief with a yes/no prompt. On “yes” it downloads the PDF, has a local LLM walk through the paper from first principles, and returns a Markdown report.

projects.name: Local RAG Document Q&A Assistant
projects.description: A fully local retrieval-augmented generation pipeline. Upload a PDF, TXT, DOCX, or MD file; it is chunked, embedded with nomic-embed-text, and stored in ChromaDB, and questions are answered by llama3.2 under a strict answer-only-from-context prompt. No cloud APIs, and no data leaves the machine.

notes.title: AI agent memory, part 2: what happens when facts change
notes.summary: Five more experiments on my personal agent's memory, checked on gpt-oss-120b. Overwriting old facts left a small model unable to notice changes, no memory design caught my outdated questions until one prompt sentence took that from 3% to 91%, and a fix for invented projects took them from 3 to 0.

notes.title: AI agent memory: 5 research based experiments on an agent with real data
notes.summary: Five experiments on two months of my real coding-session history, testing ideas from the Mem0 and MemoryTax papers on a free-tier model. Overwriting memory destroyed history; facts plus raw text plus mixed keyword and embedding search did best.

notes.title: Building a personal AI agent that keeps track of everything I work on
notes.summary: Saati is a personal AI agent I talk to on Telegram. It tracks my projects, ideas, and decisions, follows my coding sessions and voice notes, and runs in the cloud on a Gemini model.

notes.title: How does gradient descent work in AI? Loss, slopes, and the chain rule
notes.summary: A model learns by measuring how wrong it is and nudging every number towards less wrong. This note builds that from nothing: what a loss function is, what a slope really measures, why the gradient points uphill, and how the chain rule prices a weight buried ten layers deep.

notes.title: Building Aditi, a Hindi and English voice agent with Pipecat and tool calling
notes.summary: A real-time voice agent for a fictional Ahmedabad real estate agency. She searches listings, works out EMIs, books site visits, and texts a follow-up, in Hindi or English, on a laptop CPU and free tiers.

notes.title: How a neural network layer works: matrices, bias, and ReLU
notes.summary: A neural network layer is a matrix, a bias, and a nonlinearity. This note builds it from nothing: what a matrix does to a vector, why stacking linear layers collapses into a single layer, and why ReLU is what makes depth worth having.

notes.title: What are word embeddings? How text becomes vectors
notes.summary: A computer has no notion of meaning or context. This note builds word embeddings from nothing: why one number per word fails, why vectors work, and why the angle between two vectors tells you a cat is closer to a dog than to a car.

notes.title: Building AI Stack Advisor, a build-vs-buy calculator for AI
notes.summary: Should a business buy a SaaS tool, build on APIs, or run its own model? A free browser tool that answers with costs, TCO, break-even, and ROI, in your own currency and with your country's tax rules.

notes.title: Building TickerBrief, an automated equity research pipeline with n8n, Python, and a local LLM
notes.summary: Type a ticker, get a full equity research report with charts, filings, news sentiment, and an LLM-written narrative. How the data, the scorecard, and the three LLM passes work, and why the LLM never touches a number.

notes.title: Building a model drift monitor with Evidently, n8n, and a local LLM
notes.summary: A local MLOps stack that notices when a model starts going wrong and explains why, in plain English, on Slack. The metrics, the alert rules, four failure scenarios, and what the test runs showed.

notes.title: Building a fully local RAG document assistant with n8n, Ollama, and ChromaDB
notes.summary: A document Q&A assistant that runs entirely on my machine. How it splits, embeds, and retrieves text, the prompt that stops a small model from guessing, and what would change with a cloud model, different chunk sizes, or conversation memory.

notes.title: FocusPulse: a Chrome extension for tracking your own focus
notes.summary: A Chrome extension where you track your own focus in four colours. Ideas to make it more addictive are welcome.

notes.title: How AI benchmarks are actually designed, from first principles
notes.summary: Benchmarks look like simple tables of percentages. Underneath, each one is a measuring instrument with design choices about tasks, scoring, statistics, and leakage. Here is how they work.

notes.title: EasyAutoFill: a browser extension that fills any form from your own profile file
notes.summary: A local, open-source browser extension that fills any form from your own profile file.

notes.title: Starting a statistics series on Medium
notes.summary: Stats_with_FirstPrinciples: rebuilding statistical thinking from the ground up, one intuitive post at a time.

notes.title: Automating my morning arXiv routine with n8n, Telegram, and an LLM
notes.summary: Checking arXiv every day and feeding papers to an LLM ate my mornings, so I built an n8n workflow to do it. How it works, the bugs that made it silently return nothing, and how it went from a small local model to full-paper derivations.

notes.title: How machine learning and deep learning are different
notes.summary: Not "deep learning is ML with neural networks," but why. A first-principles look at what each one is really doing, and why the difference comes down to who builds the representation.

notes.title: How AI labs actually train their models
notes.summary: From raw web text to a helpful assistant: the stages every big lab goes through, and how OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta, and DeepSeek each do it differently.

notes.title: Why Karpathy said gradient descent writes better code than you
notes.summary: What Karpathy actually meant when he said gradient descent writes better code, what his Software 2.0 essay got right, and how it reads nine years on.

notes.title: How Claude overtook GPT (where it matters)
notes.summary: ChatGPT is still the household name, but in coding and enterprise use, Anthropic's Claude has caught up and pulled ahead this year. Here is how that happened.

notes.title: The maths and physics hiding inside LLMs
notes.summary: Like many others, I was surprised the physics Nobel went to Geoffrey Hinton. So I went looking for the physics and maths inside large language models.

notes.title: What is Google's NotebookLM, and how is it different from a chatbot and from RAG?
notes.summary: NotebookLM, ChatGPT, and RAG get discussed as three competing things. They are not. One is a product, one is a pattern, and the difference that actually matters is who decides what the model is allowed to read.

notes.title: What is RAG (retrieval augmented generation), and why does it matter so much?
notes.summary: Retrieval-augmented generation lets an AI answer from your own documents instead of its memory. Here is how it works, why it has become so important, and where it goes wrong.

notes.title: My quickest paper, and an unexpected collaboration
notes.summary: How a comment in a research meeting turned into a paper with Mustapha Azreg-Aïnou in about six weeks.

notes.title: GPT: the model that started it all
notes.summary: With GPT-4 out, I went back to where the GPT series began. The surprising part is how simple the core idea is, and how far scaling it went.

notes.title: ChatGPT: the interface that changed everything
notes.summary: ChatGPT is two weeks old and everyone around me is talking to it. The model behind it is not brand new. The way we get to use it is.

notes.title: Where machine learning meets black hole energy extraction
notes.summary: Machine learning doesn't calculate the Penrose process for us, but it is quietly becoming essential to everything around it.

notes.title: My first paper: stealing energy from spinning black holes (and their mimickers)
notes.summary: The Penrose process in plain words, and what my first paper found when we ran it around Kerr black hole mimickers. One family matched Kerr exactly; another was far more efficient.

notes.title: My MSc thesis: following light and matter around black holes
notes.summary: Five months of learning how light and particles move around black holes, naked singularities, and wormholes.
